title: Rate limits & org/project keys demo - Medicorp
next_steps: Send rate limit and pricing sheet
Share SOC2 / infra security pack link
Schedule 1hr pilot setup call w/ SE & Medicorp infra team
action_items: Alex Chen: send pricing + rate limit examples by 2025-03-06
Priya Iyer: prepare pilot config (org/project keys, sample policies) by 2025-03-07
Mark Rivers: share list of expected tenants and peak qps by 2025-03-10
summary: Redwood AE+SE ran a demo for Medicorp focused on rate limiting, quotas, and multi-tenant controls using org and project API keys. Customer cares about per-tenant quotas, burst behavior, audit logs, and integration with their SSO/KMS. Agreed next steps: send pricing & security docs, set up pilot with sample policies, and gather tenant traffic profiles.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros then we'll jump into the console demo.
[00:12] Mark Rivers (Medicorp CTO): hi all, Mark here - excited to see how you handle org keys, we've got multiple hospitals and each needs its own quota.
[00:20] Priya Iyer (Redwood SE): great, Mark. i'll show the Console and the Optimize recommendations and then demo how org and project keys enforce rate limits and quotas.
[00:30] Elena Park (Medicorp - Sec): hi, quick note we need audit trails and KMS integration — our security team won't accept secrets in plaintext.
[00:38] Alex: understood. we'll cover KMS and audit logs, also RBAC and SSO touches.
[00:45] Samir (Platform Eng): curious about burst limits — do you let us define token-based bursts per project?
[00:52] Priya: yes, you can set steady-state qps and a burst window; console shows adaptive throttling and leaky-bucket behavior. i'll switch to the Console now.
[01:10] (screen share starts)
[01:18] Priya: ok i have the org view, here is Medicorp (demo org). top-level settings include global throughput cap, default project quota, and enforcement policy. i created two demo projects: 'ambulatory' and 'er-cluster'.
[01:35] Priya: the project keys are under Projects -> Keys. each key maps to an org and a project scope; you can create per-project keys and tag them.
[01:50] Alex: for multi-tenant setups we recommend issuing a project key per tenant and then using rate-limiting policies tied to that key so you get clean billing and isolation.
[01:58] Mark: that aligns with what we planned. if a tenant goes noisy, can we throttle them without affecting others?
[02:05] Priya: yes — policy examples: you can set hard limits (reject after X reqs) or soft limits (throttle / queue) and fallback model variants. here is a sample policy: 20 rps steady, 100 rps burst for 60s, and then degrade to a cheaper model if sustained.
[02:30] (slight audio glitch)
[02:36] Elena: how do you surface per-tenant usage in logs? we need per-tenant entries in audit logs for compliance.
[02:44] Priya: logs include key_id, org_id, project_id, route, tokens_consumed, latency. we also emit structured events to your SIEM via webhook or cloud logging. note: sometimes the generated entity names in older exports were mis-typed but the payloads are stable.
[03:05] Samir: do you integrate with our KMS for key rotation?
[03:10] Alex: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM; for hosted we offer KMS integrations and rotation APIs.
[03:18] Jodi: procurement question — do you charge per org or per project?
[03:22] Alex: pricing is usage-based, but reserved capacity and enterprise plans can include per-project billing reports. i'll send the pricing + rate-limit examples after.
[03:30] Priya: switching to API demo now — i will show a curl example creating an API key and applying a policy.
[03:42] Priya (screen): here is POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects to create project, then POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/keys. payload sample (on-screen): {"name":"er-cluster-key","policy":"policy-123"}.
[03:58] Mark: are those policies declarative? in our infra we prefer config-as-code.
[04:02] Priya: yes, policies are YAML/JSON based and can be checked into your repo; we also have a policy API. you can use the Optimize tool to get suggestions based on traffic.
[04:18] (crosstalk)
[04:22] Priya: now i’ll demonstrate a live throttle — i'll fire a burst of simulated requests using the key for 'ambulatory' and show the console charts.
[04:35] (simulation running, beeps in background)
[04:42] Priya: you can see requests crossing the steady threshold, burst allowed up to 120 rps then we start returning 429s for that key only; other project keys remain unaffected.
[04:58] Mark: nice. what about queuing vs immediate 429? we want a short queue for occasional spikes.
[05:05] Priya: policy can be set to 'queue' up to N requests for T seconds; after that 429. also support prioritized lanes if you tag tenants with SLAs.
[05:20] Samir: does queuing impact latency SLOs?
[05:23] Priya: it can — Optimize recommends batching and cache TTLs to reduce tokens and keep latency low. you can set per-route latency SLOs and fallback rules.
[05:36] Elena: on audit logs, do you keep payloads or just metadata? our compliance only needs metadata and hashed ids.
[05:43] Alex: default stores metadata; payload capture is opt-in and encrypted, and can be sent to your storage. we support scrubbers and retention policies.
[05:55] Priya: showing the audit log sample in the Console — each line: timestamp, request_id, key_id, project_id, tokens, user_agent, rule_triggered.
[06:12] (15s silence)
[06:28] Mark: any native tenant isolation at the runtime level? or is it just logical separation?
[06:34] Priya: we have both logical isolation (project keys, per-key quotas) and dedicated pools option (Dedicated) for strict isolation. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools so noisy neighbor risk is minimized.
[06:50] Mark: for Medicorp some hospitals will require dedicated tenancy; others can be shared. can we mix?
[06:56] Alex: yes, smart routing can send certain projects to Dedicated capacity while others go to hosted. that's configured by route/policy.
[07:10] Jodi: procurement needs an SLA sample for latency and uptime.
[07:16] Alex: we'll include SLA docs in the security packet.
[07:20] Priya: demoing the policy editor now — you can create a policy that references org-level defaults and then override per-project. here is a sample YAML with rules:
[07:36] (on-screen snippet read)
[07:38] "rules:
  - match: route:/chat
    limit: 30rps
    burst: 120
    behavior: queue
    fallback: model:fast-compact"
[07:55] Mark: will fallback change model semantics? our NLU accuracy is critical for some flows.
[07:59] Priya: fallbacks are configurable — you can choose to degrade only non-critical routes or send 100% of calls but tag them. Optimize will flag quality regressions tied to prompts and evals.
[08:15] Elena: what about RBAC in Console? we need role separation for audit and no-one should be able to change policies without approval.
[08:23] Priya: Console has RBAC roles: Org Admin, Billing, Reader, Policy Editor. changes can be gated by approvals integrations with your SSO system. all changes are tracked in audit logs.
[08:40] Samir: do you provide traffic simulation tools to validate policies?
[08:45] Priya: yes, the Console has a traffic replay tool and a synthetic load generator. for pilots we can run a controlled replay against a sandbox.
[08:55] (background notification sound)
[09:02] Alex: quick pause — any blockers for Medicorp to proceed to pilot?
[09:08] Mark: need assurance on encryption, KMS, and per-tenant auditability. also need expected qps numbers.
[09:15] Alex: ok we'll send the security pack (SOC2, infra, KMS details) + request a tenant traffic spreadsheet.
[09:22] Priya: one more demo item — API rate-limits can be set at route level; you can also attach usage-based quota buckets for billing. show code snippet for checking remaining quota in response headers.
[09:40] (reads snippet)
[09:46] Priya: response headers include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset and also key-level metrics like X-Project-Quota-Remaining.
[09:58] Mark: perfect, that fits our monitoring needs.
[10:02] Jodi: procurement follow-up — is there a minimal commitment for Dedicated?
[10:07] Alex: yes Dedicated is reserve-based; we'll include committed options in the pricing doc.
[10:12] (conversation drifts into procurement details)
[10:35] Priya: bringing up Optimize now — this will recommend quantization, batching configs, and policy tweaks to meet cost/latency targets per workload.
[10:50] Priya: Optimize showed that for chat-heavy workload, 4-bit quantization + per-tenant caching reduces tokens by ~20% without visible quality regression on our evals.
[11:08] Mark: can Optimize simulate tenant-level economics? we want visibility into cost per hospital.
[11:12] Priya: yes we can break down cost by project key and show recommendations per project.
[11:20] Elena: governance question — can policy changes be audited and rolled back automatically?
[11:26] Priya: yes, Console has history + rollout controls; you can do canary policies and automatic rollback if errors spike.
[11:38] Samir: what's the expected operator effort to maintain these policies?
[11:43] Priya: depends on scale; Optimize automates many suggestions but Platform will need to review edge cases. for pilot we recommend one SE + one platform engineer.
[11:56] (short silence)
[12:10] Alex: ok quick recap of next steps and owners.
[12:15] Alex: i'll send pricing and security docs; Priya will share pilot config and sample policy YAML; Mark will provide tenant qps and list; Jodi will coordinate procurement timeline.
[12:28] Mark: thanks, this was helpful.
[12:32] Elena: happy with approach, looking forward to the SEC packet.
[12:36] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links.
[12:45] (call ends)
